purpose: A compact label with distinct static, removable, interactive, counter, and status behaviors.
behaviorProvider: Static labels or native toggle/remove actions; Chip is the same export.

component: Interactive tags render a button with aria-pressed from selected and emit onSelectedChange with its inverse; selected is host controlled.
Removable tags keep a separate named button. Click, Backspace or Delete invokes onRemove; the component itself does not remove data or choose the next focus target.
host: Keep labels short and supply contextual removeLabel values. Own selection/removal, filter behavior and focus after removing a focused tag.
Use semantic group tokens for styling and meaning-appropriate intents; do not encode application state solely as dotColor.

requirements.statement: Interactive tags render a button with aria-pressed from selected and emit onSelectedChange with its inverse; selected is host controlled.
Removable tags keep a separate named button. Click, Backspace or Delete invokes onRemove; the component itself does not remove data or choose the next focus target.
Static/counter/status variants render a span, with counter defaulting to zero. Status/intent dots are decorative. disabled affects actionable buttons.
Export Chip and ChipProps as aliases of Tag and TagProps with identical behavior.
Keep labels short and supply contextual removeLabel values. Own selection/removal, filter behavior and focus after removing a focused tag.
Use semantic group tokens for styling and meaning-appropriate intents; do not encode application state solely as dotColor.

Use data-display group tokens for owned presentation, preserve genuine nested component ownership, and verify the same geometry across Fundamental and Fundamental Floating in light/dark. Keep the documented semantics and state model when composing or extending this family.

limitations: Tags do not implement a tag input, listbox or multiselection model. Counter values are not validated.
Authored source coverage is separate from executed interaction, visual, accessibility and consumer-package evidence.
